**Language rationales**: Java speaks SR's REST surface directly (official client is Java, but CI image excludes Confluent jars — raw `java.net.http` against the documented v1 media type); Go and Python have no official REST Proxy SDK — versioned HTTP+JSON media types are the documented surface, stdlib `net/http` / `urllib` are idiomatic; C# has no official Connect management SDK — JSON REST via `HttpClient`/`System.Text.Json` for .NET ops tooling.

## Final report — Wave 8, Chunk 8A (ServiceNow REST ×4)

A shared research finding recorded in every seed's provenance: the current ServiceNow release is **Australia** (post-Zurich) — confirmed by fetching the Australia-release API reference pages on developer.servicenow.com. The catalog's API names all match current docs; no endpoint corrections were needed. One honest limitation: ServiceNow's rate-limiting doc pages are JavaScript-gated and would not render server-side, so the 429/Retry-After retry budget (3 retries) is pinned as an explicitly-labeled *local policy* in each `docs/contract.json` rather than attributed to a fetched page.

**1. py-snow-incident-sync** — project-integration, Table API (`/api/now/table`, unversioned = latest, Australia docs). Rationale: no official Python SDK exists; raw REST via stdlib urllib is the documented surface. Sources fetched: the Australia and Zurich Table API references (`developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?...c_TableAPI...`). Tests pin sysparm_query wire encoding (`%5E`/`%3D`), offset pagination (exact offsets, request count), the result envelope, error envelope → structured exceptions, 429/Retry-After via injected sleep, idempotent create-or-patch with sys_id identity, and no credential forwarding across a cross-origin redirect. Baseline smoke: fails (`ModuleNotFoundError: snow_sync`). Reference verify: PASS (7 groups). ~67 assert statements.

**2. ts-snow-attachment-upload** — project-integration, Attachment API (`POST /api/now/attachment/upload` multipart + metadata list). Rationale: no official JS/TS SDK; REST multipart with Node built-ins. Sources: Australia + Zurich Attachment API references. Tests parse real multipart on the mock (byte-exact binary with hostile boundary-like content, `uploadFile` part name, per-part Content-Type), pre-upload correlation dedupe, ambiguous-success recovery that never re-POSTs after a 502-after-store (the catalog's core behavior), true-failure re-query-then-retry, 429 direct retry, size_bytes validation. Baseline smoke: fails. Reference verify: PASS (10 tests). 71 assertions.

**3. java-snow-change-poller** — feature-integration, Table API on change_request. Working codebase ships (single-page client, JSON parser, model); the `ChangePoller`/`PollResult` feature is missing, so baseline fails to compile. Sources: Australia + Zurich Table API references. Tests pin `sysparm_display_value=false` + `sysparm_exclude_reference_link=true` (the mock serializes `{link,value}` objects otherwise), strict-`>` checkpoint boundary, checkpoint advancing only after a full paginated scan, and 401/403/exhausted-429 returning prior results with the old checkpoint. Baseline smoke: fails (compilation). Reference verify: PASS (86 runtime checks).

- [Multipart upload overview (user guide)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) — 100 MB best-practice threshold, part numbers 1–10,000, 5 MB minimum for all but the last part, consecutive part numbers starting at 1 when checksums are used, and the must-complete-or-abort rule to stop paying for stored parts.

- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-projects/ — via the Atlassian-hosted OpenAPI spec https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json (the developer.atlassian.com reference pages are rendered from it; the HTML pages were too large for WebFetch's summarizer, so I pulled the spec and the intro page directly and read the exact text)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/intro/ — the Asynchronous operations section

Key facts verified, quoting the docs:

- **The archived-project rule really is restore-then-delete**: "You can't delete a project if it's archived. To delete an archived project, restore the project and then delete it." Restore is `POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/restore` (200) — "Restores a project that has been archived or placed in the Jira recycle bin."
- **Async delete**: `POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/delete`, "transactional, that is, if part of the delete fails the project is not deleted", answering 303. The plain `DELETE` on the project resource is a separate synchronous operation (recycle-bin `enableUndo` semantics) and is never sent.
- **Intro, async operations**: the operation "will schedule an asynchronous task and return a `303 (See Other)` response, indicating the location of the queued task in the `Location` header… When the task finishes, the response object will contain the `result` field… asynchronous tasks are not guaranteed to be run in order."
- **Get task**: `GET /rest/api/3/task/{taskId}` returns `TaskProgressBeanObject` with status enum exactly `ENQUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETE, FAILED, CANCEL_REQUESTED, CANCELLED, DEAD`.

**The live docs agree with `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` on every point** — no discrepancies; fixtures left untouched. One non-conflicting nuance: the archive operation's description says "To restore a project, use the Jira UI," but the REST restore endpoint exists in the same spec and is what the workflow (and the pinned contract) uses.

## Implementation

`ProjectRetirement.purge()` does: state check via `getProject` → `POST …/restore` only if `archived` (this is what the browser-clicker got wrong — deleting while archived is the 400) → `POST …/delete` expecting 303, rejecting a missing/blank `Location` with an `IllegalStateException` that names the header → polls the Location URL up to `maxPolls` times, calling `backoff.pause(n)` only between consecutive polls. Termination keys off `status` alone, since progress/lastUpdate may legally regress. `COMPLETE` returns `Result(taskId, restored, pollCount, taskResult)`; `FAILED`/`CANCELLED`/`DEAD` raises `TaskFailedException` preserving the task's own message and stating the project was not deleted (the silent-half-failure case from last quarter now fails loudly); exhausting `maxPolls` raises `IllegalStateException("… still running …")`. Non-2xx/303 HTTP answers still raise `JiraApiException`, whose messages never carry credentials.

- `pubstream/lease.py` — `LeaseHandle.extend(seconds)` goes through `Message.modify_ack_deadline`, accepts only integers in [10, 600] (600 is the service maximum; everything below the advised 10-second floor — including the 0-second effective nack — is a ValueError), and records successes on `.extensions`.
- `pubstream/worker.py` — `StreamWorker(handler)` calls `handler(data, attributes_dict, lease)` and acks only after it returns; a raising handler gets exactly one nack, no ack, `(message_id, exception)` on `.failures`, and the exception never escapes the callback. `.acked`/`.nacked` track ids in order.
- `pubstream/runner.py` — `StreamRunner` builds the subscription path via the injected subscriber, calls `subscribe()` with the configured flow control and `await_callbacks_on_shutdown` forwarded verbatim, returns the StreamingPullFuture from `start()`, raises RuntimeError on double-start or stop-before-start, and `stop(timeout=...)` does `cancel()` then `result(timeout)` in the documented order.

- **java-globpat** vs existing `ts-reglob`/`go-globmatch`/`py-glob-match`: differentiated by layer and API surface — it's a rename planner, not just a matcher: `Pattern.quote` islands that must survive embedded `\E`/`\Q` text, wildcards as capturing groups, and `{n}` rename templates where `$`/`\` replacement-syntax leakage is the tested failure mode.

router is exact-match only and the gateway team is stuck. Need pattern routing:

- ":name" segments capture one path segment ("/repos/:owner/:repo")
- "*name" as the FINAL segment captures the whole non-empty remainder including slashes; "*" anywhere else, or unnamed "*"/":", is a registration error via a sentinel ErrInvalidPattern
- new Match(path) returning (handler, Params, ok) where Params is the captures map
- precedence when several patterns fit, decided per segment left to right: static beats :param beats *wildcard (so /api/users/:id wins over /api/:section/stats for /api/users/stats)

Handle/Lookup/List keep their exact current semantics — Lookup stays a literal string lookup, no pattern smarts. params_test.go is the acceptance contract, router_test.go pins today's behavior, hands off both test files. Green = go test -race -timeout 30s ./...
output:
FIKIR: I'll look at the current router implementation and tests first.

JAWAPAN AKHIR:
Green — `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...` passes, with both `params_test.go` (the new acceptance contract) and `router_test.go` (existing behavior) intact. All changes are in router.go:

- **`Match(path) (H, Params, bool)`** — `router.go:129`. Normalizes the path the same way `Lookup` does, then scans the parsed routes and keeps the best fit. Params is a `map[string]string` of captures, allocated lazily so exact matches return nil.
- **Pattern parsing at registration** — `Handle` now runs `parsePattern` (`router.go:87`) before storing anything, so an invalid pattern is rejected atomically and never becomes routable. `ErrInvalidPattern` is the sentinel; it covers unnamed `:`/`*` segments, a `*` segment that isn't last, and `*` appearing anywhere other than the start of the final segment (e.g. `/a/b*c`).
- **Precedence** — each pattern is a sequence of segment kinds (static=0, param=1, wildcard=2), and `better` compares two fitting patterns' kind sequences lexicographically left to right, which is exactly the "decided per segment" rule: `/api/users/:id` (static, static, param) beats `/api/:section/stats` (static, param, static) for `/api/users/stats`. Since a wildcard can only be final, two fitting patterns always align position by position. Exact ties (e.g. `/a/:x` vs `/a/:y`) go to the first registered.
- **Wildcards** — `*name` requires a non-empty remainder (`matches` at `router.go:158` demands at least one segment past it) and captures it with slashes rejoined.

`Handle`/`Lookup`/`List` are untouched semantically: `Lookup` is still a literal map hit (so `Lookup("/api/users/:id")` finds the pattern itself and `Lookup("/api/users/42")` misses), duplicate detection is still by normalized literal string, and `List` still returns registration order.

One design note: `Match` is a linear scan over registered routes rather than a trie. For a gateway route table that's simple, obviously correct, and plenty fast; if the table ever grows to thousands of routes, the parsed-segment representation converts to a trie without touching the public API.

this directory. Everything below is mandatory.

 self-check. It is the law.

 `tasks/WAVE4_USECASES.md` — wave-4 extensions (loopback HTTP allowed for
 web seeds, sqlite3 allowed where SQL serves the task, refactor/perf seed
 mechanics, repo-scale sizing).

 (e.g. `tasks/seeds/py-cron-next` for build, `tasks/seeds/py-tree-filters`
 for feature; `ls tasks/seeds/` and pick something close).

## Scope and etiquette

- `ls tasks/seeds/` FIRST. Your ids must be new (`<lang>-<slug>`), your
 domains must not re-skin an existing seed — when the catalog's angle
 overlaps an existing seed, differentiate sharply (different layer,
 different API surface) and say so in a comment in your final report.
- Touch ONLY `tasks/seeds/<your-ids>/` and `workspaces/<your-ids>/`. Never
 edit `src/`, `config.json`, other seeds, PROGRESS.md, or
